Hi Markus,

Thanks for the quick follow-up after the RFP review — we'd love to see Redwood in action. Our team in New York is generally available during US business hours (09:30–17:30 ET). I know your core engineering team is in Berlin, and we want to be mindful of late hours.

Two constraints on our side: 1) prefer no meetings starting earlier than 09:30 ET, and 2) avoid running past 21:00 local for any Redwood attendees.

If helpful, here are some candidate slots from our side next week (we're flexible):
- Wed Sep 2: 14:00 ET / 20:00 CEST
- Thu Sep 3: 11:00 ET / 17:00 CEST
- Fri Sep 4: 10:00 ET / 16:00 CEST

We can do a 45–60 minute demo + Q&A. Also happy to record if a portion needs to be asynchronous. Can you confirm whether your product/solutions engineering team can join one of those windows, or if we should propose alternate times?

Thanks,

Thanks Caroline — really appreciate the constraints. Looping in Laura (solutions) and Kimberly (eng lead) so we can confirm with the Berlin team. Laura/Kimberly — quick context: Midtown wants a 45–60m walkthrough focused on dedicated inference economics and live Q&A. Preferred windows listed below from the customer.

Quick notes on scheduling tradeoffs:
- Thu Sep 3 11:00 ET / 17:00 CEST is a solid mid-afternoon option for Berlin and mid-day for NYC.
- Wed Sep 2 14:00 ET / 20:00 CEST would push Berlin to late evening (still doable but we'd prefer to avoid regular late-night calls).

Two compromises I recommend (so we don't force our EU team into an uncomfortable late slot):
Option A — Earlier EU, later US (shorter overlap):
- Fri Sep 4, 10:00 ET / 16:00 CEST — good for Berlin engineers and within Midtown hours.

Option B — Mid-afternoon US, polite evening EU (one-time exception):
- Wed Sep 2, 14:00 ET / 20:00 CEST — can do if Midtown prefers an exec-friendly time. We'll staff with a smaller engineering panel and offer a recording.

If Caroline/Tom prefer an exact date, we'll send a calendar invite and attach the mutual action plan (MAP). Also noting DST is stable across these dates (no clock changes until November), so offsets should be consistent.

—Markus
